title: MiniCall
summary: A call that continues while people do something else is shown in the system's picture-in-picture window. Monarch ships no floating call window.
whenToUse: To keep a call visible when the person leaves the call screen or the app. For a video call, create the controller with AVPictureInPictureController.ContentSource(activeVideoCallSourceView:contentViewController:).
whenNotToUse: Do not build a draggable in-app window; it cannot leave the app and duplicates the system one. For an audio-only call the system's call indicator in the status bar or Dynamic Island is enough.

states.name: not supported
states.description: isPictureInPictureSupported() is false; offer no button.

states.name: possible
states.description: isPictureInPicturePossible is true while there is video to show.

states.name: active
states.description: The system window floats above the app and other apps, with its own controls, and can be dragged to a corner or hidden at the edge.

appearance: System appearance in every theme. The button that starts it is an ordinary Monarch button.
platformNotes: The web MiniCall is a draggable in-page window with a timer, mute, expand and leave. Android uses its own picture-in-picture mode. On iOS the system draws the window and its controls; mute and leave stay in the app's call screen and in the system call controls. The app needs the Audio, AirPlay, and Picture in Picture background mode.
accessibility: System behaviour: the picture-in-picture window is accessible and can be moved and closed with VoiceOver.
Give the button that starts it a title or an accessibility label.
edgeCases: Picture in picture starts only while isPictureInPicturePossible is true, which needs a layer that is showing video.
The video-call content source (iOS 15) needs UIKit: a source UIView and an AVPictureInPictureVideoCallViewController.
Keep a strong reference to the controller while the window is open.
The example and the catalogue page were compiled but the window was not run.

examples.title: Inline

parityExceptions.reason: The web mini call is a floating tile; native floats a call as system picture-in-picture (AVPictureInPictureController, started by the app with its own call layer), so no Monarch view is the floating window. The example draws the same tile, with the same speaker, timer, count and mute, expand and leave controls, from Monarch parts.
